diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then there exists a constant $\zeta > 0$ such that for every $z \in \cS$, one can find a point $y \in \cY$ (possibly depending on $z$) satisfying $\bc(y, z) \leq -\zeta$.
there exists some $\tz \in \cY$ such that $\langle \nabla c_{j}(z), \tz-z \rangle < 0$

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion is a vector inequality: every component of c̄(y,z) is at most −ζ. Its negation only says that for every y some component j, which may depend on y, exceeds −ζ_k. The proof instead fixes one j that works for all y and all k. A subsequence can remove the dependence on k but not on y. The contradiction is then derived for that single constraint alone, so for m>1 the argument does not refute the actual negation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Argue with max_j c̄_j. In the limit, max_j c̄_j(y,z) ≥ 0 for all y in Y. Take the MFCQ point ỹ that works simultaneously for all active j, and note that inactive constraints satisfy c̄_j(z,z)=c_j(z)<0. Then y(t)=z+t(ỹ−z) makes all components negative for small t>0, which is a contradiction.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform Slater constant ζ is not validly established. ζ enters the multiplier bounds A and A_f and, through them, all SCP and outer complexity results.
issues.title: Invalid negation in the uniform Slater argument (single fixed constraint index)
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and a short local rewrite using MFCQ's common direction fixes the proof. No result or constant changes.

Suppose that Assumptions \ref{ass:Lip_Smo_KL} and \ref{ass:MFCQ} hold. Then the total number of evaluations

issues.failure_explanation: A_f, ω_f, α_f and the bound K̄_{f,θ} require G_f = sup over X×Y of ‖∇_y f‖ to be finite. Assumptions 1–2 allow unbounded X = dom p. For example, f(x,y)=xy with Y=[−1,1] and p=0 satisfies Assumption 1(i) but has G_f=∞. Then A_f=ω_f=∞, α_f=0, and the stated bound is undefined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis G_f < ∞ (e.g., X bounded) to Theorem thm:operations and to the corresponding complexity claims.
issues.overall_effect: The oracle complexity bound is unsupported for problems with unbounded ∇_y f over X×Y, for example when X is unbounded.
issues.title: Oracle complexity theorem uses A_f without assuming G_f < ∞
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard boundedness condition, already used in the supporting lemma, keeps the method, the rate, and the proof intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, subproblem~\eqref{surro_argmin} is a relatively simple convex optimization problem, and its optimal solution $z^{k+1,i}$ along with the associated optimal Lagrange multiplier $\lambda^{k,i}$ can typically be computed efficiently.
The functions $p, q$ are proper closed convex, and the proximal operators of $p$ and $q$ can be computed exactly.

issues.failure_explanation: Each x-update is the prox of p+δ_{B(x^k,r)}, not of p. Each SCP step (surro_argmin) minimizes q plus a quadratic over an intersection of m balls and must also return its Lagrange multiplier. Neither is a single prox evaluation of p or q, and neither is covered by Assumption 1(ii). The counting argument bounds the number of subproblem solves, not prox evaluations.

failure_location.quote: Then the total number of evaluations of the proximal operators of $p$ and $q$, and the gradient $\nabla f$ performed by Algorithm~\ref{algo_implement:whole} is at most $\widehat{K}_\epsilon$, $\widehat{N}_\epsilon$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume an exact oracle for the ball-constrained prox of p and for subproblem (surro_argmin) with its multiplier. Restate the counts as numbers of such subproblem solves, or analyze the inner solver's cost.
issues.overall_effect: The stated prox-evaluation counts for p and q, and the exact implementability of Algorithms 1–2 under the stated assumptions, are unsupported. The gradient-evaluation count is unaffected.
issues.title: Constrained subproblems counted as single proximal-operator evaluations
issues.why_classification: The repair either changes the guarantee type (subproblem-oracle calls instead of prox evaluations) or requires a new inner-solver analysis. The gradient-complexity headline survives.
